correctness.rationale: For every ordered pair the four third-vertex adjacency cells have the displayed SRG parameter counts. The third move in a three-pebble-free EF game only tests zero versus positive; all six positivity predicates are realized as existential rank-three witnesses. The classical parameter equation and primitive/imprimitive split exhaust all 12 realizable profiles. Sharpness at order ten follows from parity and the exact irreducible spectral obstruction to (9,4,0,3), with the Petersen example attaining the lower bound. Full q3-type recursion on 18 actual graph constructions agrees independently; the symbolic proof handles all finite orders.

value.rationale: This yields a complete natural logical invariant at the first quantifier rank capable of separating nontrivial strongly regular graphs: one rank-two class becomes exactly twelve rank-three classes across primitive, imprimitive, disconnected, and nontransitive examples. The six-cell test is reusable and constructive; the sharp ten-vertex kernel realizes a complete finite logical quotient. This is not merely a new parameter table or one-family exercise and is motivated by EF expressivity for symmetric graph classes.
